name: What Remains in the Floodmark
description: A flat-screen documentary compiled from eleven years of covert footage by journalist-filmmaker Priya Anand-Sørensen documenting the systematic displacement of Shelf communities to make way for Tier 3 infrastructure expansion in the city's eastern corridor. The film includes intercepted internal communications from three corponations and testimony from forty-six residents, most of whom have since been relocated or disappeared. It exists in no licensed format and has never been screened publicly in any corponation territory.
cultural_impact: Copies distributed via physical media and dead drops have made it arguably the most-discussed banned film in M88's underground press, though most people have only heard descriptions rather than seen it.
story_hooks: Anand-Sørensen is rumored to still be in Meridian 88, editing a sequel — and someone in the corponation intelligence apparatus wants her found before it releases.
One of the forty-six witnesses in the film approaches the players claiming their testimony was included without full consent and they now fear for their life.
A physical copy of the film is hidden inside a wall cavity in a building scheduled for demolition in forty-eight hours.
